The Living World.question: [NEET 2021 | Biology] The correct sequence of taxonomic hierarchy from highest to lowest is:

options.A: Kingdom \u₂₁₉₂ Phylum \u₂₁₉₂ Class \u₂₁₉₂ Order \u₂₁₉₂ Family \u₂₁₉₂ Genus \u₂₁₉₂ Species
options.B: Kingdom \u₂₁₉₂ Class \u₂₁₉₂ Phylum \u₂₁₉₂ Order \u₂₁₉₂ Family \u₂₁₉₂ Genus \u₂₁₉₂ Species
options.C: Species \u₂₁₉₂ Genus \u₂₁₉₂ Family \u₂₁₉₂ Order \u₂₁₉₂ Class \u₂₁₉₂ Phylum \u₂₁₉₂ Kingdom
options.D: Kingdom \u₂₁₉₂ Phylum \u₂₁₉₂ Order \u₂₁₉₂ Class \u₂₁₉₂ Family \u₂₁₉₂ Genus \u₂₁₉₂ Species

The Living World.solution: # Correct Answer: **(A) Kingdom \u₂₁₉₂ Phylum \u₂₁₉₂ Class \u₂₁₉₂ Order \u₂₁₉₂ Family \u₂₁₉₂ Genus \u₂₁₉₂ Species** --- ## Step-by-Step Explanation The taxonomic hierarchy follows a **nested classification system** where each level becomes progressively more specific: | Rank | Level | Breadth | Example | |------|-------|---------|---------| | 1 | **Kingdom** | Broadest | Animalia | | 2 | **Phylum** | \u₂₁₉₃ | Chordata | | 3 | **Class** | \u₂₁₉₃ | Mammalia | | 4 | **Order** | \u₂₁₉₃ | Primates | | 5 | **Family** | \u₂₁₉₃ | Hominidae | | 6 | **Genus** | \u₂₁₉₃ | Homo | | 7 | **Species** | Narrowest | sapiens | --- ## Memory Aid (Mnemonic) **"King Philip Came Over For Good Soup"** - **K**ing, **P**hilip, **C**ame, **O**ver, **F**or, **G**ood, **S**oup - Helps remember: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong - **(B)**: Incorrectly places Class before Phylum - wrong sequence - **(C)**: This is completely reversed (Species to Kingdom instead of Kingdom to Species) - **(D)**: Incorrectly places Order before Class - violates the correct hierarchical order --- ## Key Concept to Remember \u₂₇₁₃ **Taxonomic hierarchy moves from the most general (Kingdom) to the most specific (Species)** \u₂₇₁₃ Each organism belongs to exactly one taxon at each level \u₂₇₁₃ The lower you go in the hierarchy, the fewer organisms share those characteristics

Biological Classification.question: [NEET 2022 | Biology] Which organisms are responsible for nitrogen fixation in legume root nodules?
Biological Classification.solution: # Answer: **(B) Rhizobium** ## Step-by-Step Explanation ### The Nitrogen Fixation Process in Legumes: 1. **Symbiotic Relationship**: Rhizobium bacteria form a mutualistic symbiosis with legume plants (beans, peas, clover, etc.) 2. **Root Nodule Formation**: - Rhizobium enters legume root hairs - Stimulates formation of root nodules - Bacteria occupy specialized compartments within nodule cells 3. **Nitrogen Fixation**: - Rhizobium uses the enzyme **nitrogenase** to convert atmospheric N\u₂₀₈₂ to NH\u₂₀₈₃ - Plant provides carbohydrates for bacterial energy - Bacteria provide fixed nitrogen compounds to plant ## Why Other Options Are Wrong: | Option | Why It's Wrong | |--------|---| | **(A) Azotobacter** | Free-living nitrogen fixers in soil, NOT in root nodules | | **(C) Nitrosomonas** | Nitrifying bacteria that convert NH\u₂₀₈₃ \u₂₁₉₂ NO\u₂₀₈₂\u₂₀₇b, not fixers | | **(D) Pseudomonas** | General soil bacteria; some strains fix nitrogen but not in legume nodules | ## Key Concept to Remember: **Rhizobium + Legumes = Nitrogen-fixing Nodules** This is the most important nitrogen fixation partnership in agriculture. Legume crops (pulses) naturally enrich soil with nitrogen without synthetic fertilizers! **Formula**: N\u₂₀₈₂ \u₂₁₉₂ NH\u₂₀₈₃ (via nitrogenase enzyme in Rhizobium)
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: [NEET 2021 | Biology] Mycorrhizal association between fungi and plant roots is an example of:
Biological Classification.solution: # Answer: **(C) Mutualism** ## Step-by-Step Reasoning: ### Understanding Mycorrhizal Association: Mycorrhizal fungi form associations with plant roots where fungal hyphae: - Penetrate the root cells (or surround them) - Create an extensive network in the soil ### Benefits to Each Organism: **Benefits to the Plant:** - Enhanced absorption of water and minerals (especially phosphorus, nitrogen, and other micronutrients) - Improved nutrient uptake from nutrient-poor soils - Better drought tolerance - Increased growth and survival **Benefits to the Fungus:** - Obtains organic compounds and carbohydrates (sugars) from plant photosynthesis - Gets a steady source of nutrition ## Key Concept: Since **both organisms gain benefits** from the association, this is **MUTUALISM** \— the most beneficial symbiotic relationship. ## Why Other Options Are Wrong: | Relationship | Definition | Why it's wrong | |---|---|---| | **Parasitism (A)** | One benefits, one is harmed | Both organisms benefit here | | **Commensalism (B)** | One benefits, other unaffected | The plant definitely benefits | | **Amensalism (D)** | One harmed, other unaffected | Both benefit, not harmed | ## Key Formula/Fact to Remember: **Mycorrhizae = Mutual benefit = MUTUALISM** - Examples: N\u₂₀₈₂-fixing bacteria with legumes, algae with fungi (lichen)
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: [NEET 2017 | Biology] Which shows coiled RNA strand and protein units?
Biological Classification.solution: ## Correct Answer: **(B) Tobacco mosaic virus** --- ## Step-by-Step Explanation: **Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV) Structure:** - Has a **helical/coiled arrangement** of single-stranded RNA - Surrounded by **coat protein subunits** arranged helically - The RNA forms a spiral strand at the center - Protein units (\u₂₂₄₈₂,130 identical subunits) wrap around this RNA in a precise helical manner - Creates a rod-like or filamentous appearance ( 300 nm long) --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong: | Virus | Reason | |-------|--------| | **Bacteriophage** | Contains DNA (not RNA); has icosahedral or complex head-tail structure, not helical | | **Measles virus** | Enveloped virus with helical nucleocapsid, but not the characteristic simple coiled RNA-protein display | | **Polio virus** | Non-enveloped RNA virus with **icosahedral symmetry** (20-sided), not helical structure | --- ## Key Concept to Remember: **Viral Symmetry Types:** - **Helical symmetry**: RNA/DNA coiled with protein subunits arranged helically \u₂₁₉₂ TMV, Influenza (nucleocapsid) - **Icosahedral symmetry**: 20-sided geometric structure \u₂₁₉₂ Polio, Measles, Adenovirus - **Complex symmetry**: Head + tail structure \u₂₁₉₂ Bacteriophages **TMV was historically the first virus discovered and remains the classic example of helical symmetry in NEET biology.**
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** Commonly known forms of class-Basidiomycetes are mushroom, bracket fungi or puffballs. According to a view for the nature of association in lichen, the relationship between fungus and the algal partner, is an example of symbiosis but fungus in his partnership has an important role. The algal partner lives as a subordinate partner the association between the two partners is thus, described as beneficial salavary for the alga. A term helotism is used for this kind of association.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: St. Anthony’s fire disease is caused by
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** St. Anthony’s fire disease is caused by ingesting rye flour containing poisons produced by a fungus 𝐶𝑙𝑎𝑣𝑖𝑐𝑒𝑝𝑠.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: In 𝑃𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑢𝑚, signet ring stage us formed during
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** During erythrocytic schizogony, micro metacryptomerozoites enter into the blood stream and each enters the red blood corpuscles and assumes rounded disc-like shape with single nucleus.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: The parthenospores of 𝑅ℎ𝑖𝑧𝑜𝑝𝑢𝑠 are
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** In 𝑅ℎ𝑖𝑧𝑜𝑝𝑢𝑠, sexual reproduction takes place by the fusion of two multinucleate gametangia. Occasionally, fusion does not take place between gametangia and these gametangia are surrounded by a many layered wall and then develop into multinucleate azygospores (parthenospore).
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Which of these best describes the saprophytic generation in plant’s life cycle?

options.D: Generation that has xylem and phloem

Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** Sporophyte stage The spore producing phase in the life cycle of a plant that exhibits alternation of generations

Biological Classification.question: Fruiting body of 𝑃𝑒𝑛𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑖𝑢𝑚 is
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** A closed fruit or ascocarp is called the cleistothecium. The cleistothecium of 𝑃𝑒𝑛𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑖𝑢𝑚 repesents parent haplophase, dikaryophase and future haplophase.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Plants have a/an…… in their life cycle
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** Life cycle of plants has two distinct phase, the haploid gametophyte and diploid sporophyte generations that alternates with each other
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Which is false for nutrition in 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎is not a photoautotrophic animal instead it takes food from their surroundings. 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎is an omnivorous animals because it takes algae, bacteria and other similar microorganisms. It takes food with the help of pseudopodia. Food particles are taken by endocytosis process, 𝑖. 𝑒., holozoic nutrition.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: …… give the name virus, which means venom or poisonous fluid Fill in the blank
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** The name virus that means venous or poisonous fluid was given by Pasteur. DJ Ivanowsky (1892) recognised certain microbes as causal organism of the mosaic disease of tobacco
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: I. 𝑁𝑜𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑙𝑢𝑐𝑎 is a colourless dinoflagellates, which is an important constituent of coastal plankton of both temperate and tropical seas II. The cellular slime moulds have the characters of both plants and animals Which of the statements given above is/ are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** Noctiluca (the night light) is a colourless dinoflagelate, which is an important constituent of coastal plankton of both temperature and tropical seas. This alga is famous for bioluminescence as it was the first dinoflagellate where bioluminescence was reported. The cellular slime moulds have the characters of both plants and animals. The reproductive phase is plant-like, as the spores have a cell wall composed of cellulose. However, vegetative phase is animal like having no cell wall and feeding like Amoeba
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Consider the following statements I. Fruce discovered that the parasite of sleeping sickness is transmitted by tse-tse fly II. Sleeping sickness of 𝑇𝑟𝑦𝑝𝑎𝑛𝑜𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑎 𝑔𝑎𝑚𝑏𝑖𝑒𝑛𝑠 is also called Gambian trypanoomiasis, which is found in western and central parts of Africa III. 𝑇𝑟𝑖𝑐ℎ𝑜𝑚𝑜𝑛𝑎𝑠 𝑣𝑎𝑔𝑖𝑛𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑠 inhabits vagina of women and causes the disease leucorrhoea IV. 𝐸𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 ℎ𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑙𝑦𝑡𝑖𝑐𝑎 resides in the upper part of the human large intestine and cause the disease known as amoebic dysentery Which of the statements given above are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** All are correct. The members of flagellated protozoans are either free living or parasitic. They bears flagella. The parasitic forms of flagellated protozoans causes diseases such as sleeping sickness, 𝑒. 𝑔., Trypanosoma
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Protozoans are divided into…… groups. Most suitable word to fill the blank is
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** On the basis of locomotory organelles, the protozoans are divided into four groups. Flagellated protozoans, amoeboid protozoans, sporozoans and ciliated protozoans
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Passive food ingestion in 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 is known as
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Import is the process in which food is sucked by depression into the body and there is no active role or movement of 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 takes place.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Consider the following statements I. Biological classification is the scientific ordering of organisms in a hierarchial series of groups on the basis of their relationships, 𝑖. 𝑒., morphological, evolutionary and others II. Whittaker classified organisms on the basis of autotrophic and heterotrophic mode of nutrition III. In five kingdom system of classification, living organisms can be divided into prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells on the basis of cell structure Which of the statements given above are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** Biological classification is the scientific procedure of arranging organisms, into groups and sub- groups on the basis of their similarities and dissimilarities and placing the groups in a hierarchy of categories Whittaker has used five criteria for delimiting the different kingdoms (i) Complexity of cell structure, i.e., prokaryotic and eukaryotic (ii) Complexity of body structure or structural organisation of unicellular and multicellular (iii) Mode of nutrition, which is divergent in multicellular kingdoms, photoautotrophy in Plantae, absorptive heterotrophy in Fungi and ingestive heterotrophy in Animalia (iv) Ecological life style like producers (Plantae) decomposers (Fungi) and consumer (Animalia) (v) Phylogenetic relationships
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Dinoflagellates are mostly ….A… and …B…. Here A and B refers to
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** The dinoflagellates are important component of phytoplankton. Most of them are marine but some occur in freshwater. Nutrition is photosynthetic in dinoflagellates
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Consider the following statements I. Diatomite is porous and chemically inert. It is therefore, used in filtration of sugar, alcohols, oils, syrups and antibiotics II. Diatomite deposits are often accompanied by petroleum fields III. Desmids are mainly found in dirty water and are, usually indication of polluted water Which of the statements given above are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** All are correct except III. Desmids are mainly found in freshwater and are usually indication of clean (unpolluted) water
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: The chief advantages of encystment of an 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 is

options.B: The chance to get rid of accumulated waste products
options.C: The ability to survive during adverse physical conditions
options.D: The ability to live sometime without ingesting food

Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** Encystment of 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 is occurred regularly to tide over unfavorable conditions like drought and extreme temperature, etc.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: During unfavourable conditions, slime mould forms …A… which are …B… and survive for many years Identify A and B to complete the given statement
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** A-spores; B-highly resistant. Slime mould forms an aggregation called Plasmodium, which may grow and spread over several feets. During unfavourable conditions, the Plasmodium differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips. Spores are extremely resistant and survive for many years
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Term ‘virus’ means
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** The name virus that means venom or poisonous fluid was given Pasteur
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: The infective stage of 𝐸𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 ℎ𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑙𝑦𝑡𝑖𝑐𝑎, is
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** In 𝐸𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 ℎ𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑙𝑦𝑡𝑖𝑐𝑎, the tetranucleate cysts constitute the transmissive or infective stage, which do not develop further but pass out from the host in faeces. These are highly resistant to desiccation and survive for about 12 days. Their infection depends upon the intake of contaminated food or water.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: ‘T-series bacteriophage’ can be recognized by its
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** T-series bacteriophages, in their appearance resemble a tadpole or spermatozoid and are differentiated into a head and a tail.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: In Whittaker’s system of classification prokaryotes are placed in the kingdom
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** RH Whittakerdivided living organisms into five kingdoms. Out of these, Monerainclude prokaryotes (bacteria, archaebacteria and cyanobacteria.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: I. Commonly known as sac-fungi II. Mycelium is branched and septate III. Conidiophore produces conidia exogenously in chain IV. The fructifications are edible and considered delicacies V. 𝑁𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑜𝑠𝑝𝑜𝑟𝑎 𝑐𝑟𝑎𝑠𝑠𝑎 is often employed in studies conducted in experimental genetics The above statements are assigned to
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Ascomycetes (Gk. askos=sac; mycete=fungus) are a large group with over 30,000 species, includes diverse types such as brown, green, blue and pink moulds, powdery mildews, yeast, morels and truffles. The mycelium is well developed and branched. The hyphae are septate and multicellular. Majority of Ascomycetes reproduce asexually by the formation of conidia. Conidia are borne on special hyphae, called conidiophores. The fructification of some Ascomycetes are edible and considered as delicacies e.g., morels, truffles. Neurospora crassa is often employed in studies conducted in experimental genetics. It is often called Drosophila of plant kingdom
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: The protistan cell body contains I. a well defined nucleus II. membrane bound cell organelles III. flagella or cilia Correct statement among those written above is
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** Protists are distinctly microscopic unicellular organisms. The cell structure is typically eukaryotic. Internally, the cells have distinct membrane bound organelles like nucleus with chromosome, mitochondria, Golgi bodies, endoplasmic reticulum, ribosomes (80S), etc. The nucleus consists of chromatin, nucleolus and nucleoplasm surrounded by porous nuclear envelope. Some motile protists may have flagella or cilia for locomotion
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: In protozoans like 𝐴𝑚𝑒𝑜𝑏𝑎 and 𝑃𝑎𝑟𝑎𝑚𝑒𝑐𝑖𝑢𝑚, which of the following organelle is found for osmoregulation?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Unicellular organisms such as 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎, 𝑃𝑎𝑟𝑎𝑚𝑒𝑐𝑖𝑢𝑚 use organelles called contractile vacuoles for osmoregulation.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Early leaf spot disease in 𝐴𝑟𝑎𝑐ℎ𝑖𝑠 ℎ𝑦𝑝𝑜𝑔𝑒𝑎 is caused due to infection of
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Causing Organism Diseases 𝑃ℎ𝑦𝑡𝑜𝑝ℎ𝑡ℎ𝑜𝑟𝑎 𝑖𝑛𝑓𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑛𝑠 Late blight of potato 𝐺𝑖𝑏𝑏𝑒𝑟𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑎 𝑓𝑢𝑗𝑖𝑘𝑢𝑟𝑜𝑖 Foolish seedling disease of rice 𝐶𝑒𝑟𝑐𝑜𝑠𝑝𝑜𝑟𝑎 𝑝𝑒𝑟𝑠𝑜𝑛𝑎𝑡𝑎 Tikka disease of groundnut 𝐴𝑔𝑟𝑜𝑏𝑎𝑐𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑖𝑢𝑚 𝑡𝑢𝑚𝑒𝑓𝑎𝑐𝑖𝑒𝑛𝑠 Crown gall disease of grapes
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Which of the following are correct to describe viruses? I. Simple and unicellular organism. II. Contain DNA or RNA and enclosed by protein coat. III. Possess own metabolic system and respond to stimuli. IV. Maintain genetic continuity and undergo mutations. The correct combination is
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** Viruses are acellular, non-cytoplasmic structures and do not have own metabolic system because enzymes are absent. These have DNA or RNA and use host metabalic system.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝑃𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑢𝑚 is a

Biological Classification.question: Life cycle of 𝑃𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑢𝑚 is
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** 𝑃𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑢𝑚 (Malaria parasite) is digenetic, 𝑖. 𝑒., completed life cycle on two hosts (man and mosquito).
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Contractile vacuole in protozoan 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 is ment for
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** Contractile vacuole is the clear rounded pulsating body present in the posterior part of endoplasm of 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎. It ais found only in fresh water forms and is mainly concerned with osmoregulation, 𝑖. 𝑒., removal of excess of water.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝑇𝑟𝑦𝑝𝑎𝑛𝑜𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑎 causes
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Trypanosome gambiense was first observed by Forde in 1901. Fruce discovered that the parasite of sleeping sickness is transmitted by tse-tse fly. It causes gambian sleeping sickness
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Assign the following substances to the cell wall, flagella, ‘S’ layer and pilli of bacteria in correct sequence. I. Glycoprotein II. Fimbrilin III. Teichoic acid IV. Flagellin The correct sequence is
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** Column I Column II Fimbrillin Pili Flagellin Flagella Teichoic acid Cell wall Glycoprotein S layer
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝐶𝑢𝑠𝑐𝑢𝑡𝑎 is a
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Cuscuta is a parasitic plant. It has no chlorophyll and cannot make its own food by photosynthesis. Instead, it grows on other plants using their nutrients for its growth and weakening the host plant
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝑃𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑢𝑚
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Plasmodium is a sporozoan and a causative agent of malarian disease. It is an endoparasite (present with in the body) and intercullar parasite

Biological Classification.question: Man in the life cycle of 𝑃𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑢𝑚, is
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** 𝑃𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑢𝑚is a digenetic protozoan, which requires two hosts, 𝑖. 𝑒., primary (man), definitive or principal host and a secondary (mosquito), intermediate or vector host.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Which of the following statements about 𝐸𝑢𝑔𝑙𝑒𝑛𝑎 is true?

options.B: Euglena when placed in continuous darkness, losses their photosynthetic activity and die
options.C: The pigments of Euglena are quite different from those of green plants P a g e | 23

Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Euglenoids are unicellular flagellate protists. Euglenoids occurs in freshwater habitats. They contains the photosynthetic pigments, chorophyll- a, chlorophyll-b, β-carotene and xanthophylls
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Baker’s yeast is
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** 𝑆𝑎𝑐𝑐ℎ𝑎𝑟𝑜𝑚𝑦𝑐𝑒𝑠 𝑐𝑒𝑟𝑒𝑣𝑖𝑠𝑖𝑎𝑒 (yeast) is commonly known as baker’s yeast or brewer’s yeast because it is widely used in baking and brewing industries.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: NH₃ in 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 is excreted by
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** Contractile vacuoles are osmoregulatory organs in 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 for the elimination of excess water from the body and excretory by-product, 𝑖. 𝑒., ammonia.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: The infective stage of 𝑃𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑢𝑚 to man, is
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** The infective stage of 𝑃𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑢𝑚 to man is sporozoite. The sporozoites are small, spindle- shaped, slightly curved and uninucleate organisms. 𝐴𝑛𝑜𝑝ℎ𝑒𝑙𝑒𝑠contains the infective stage in its salivary glands. These are transmitted during the blood meal feeding of a 𝐴𝑛𝑜𝑝ℎ𝑒𝑙𝑒𝑠 mosquito on a human.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: State whether the given statements are true or false I. Bacteria shows both autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition II. Some of the bacteria are autotrophic. They may be photosynthetic autotrophic or chemosynthetic autotrophic III. Heterotrophic nutrition involves the obtaining of readymade organic nutrients from outside sources

options.B: I is true, II and III is false
options.C: I, II and III are true

Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** Bacteria shows both autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition. Autotrophic nutrition involves manufacturing of organic materials from inorganic raw materials with the help of energy obtained from outside. It is of two types, chemosynthesis and photosynthesis. The bacteria performing these modes of nutrition are respectively called chemoautotrophs and photoautotrophs. The vast majority of bacteria are heterotrophs, i.e., they do not synthesise their own food but depends on other organism or on dead organic matter for food
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Which of the following is photoautotrophic bacteria?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Nostoc and Anabaena Cyanobacteria have chlorophyll-a, similar to green plants and are photosynthetic autotrophs. Some of these organisms can fix atmospheric nitrogen in toe specialized cells called heterocysts, 𝑒. 𝑔., Nostoc and Anabaena
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Protists are I. Unicellular and prokaryote II. Unicellular and eukaryote III. Multicellular and eukaryote IV. Autotroph or heterotroph
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** A five kingdom division oforganisms was proposed by Whittaker. Protista is one of that division. It is a kingdom of unicellular, eukaryotic organisms. Many of them are photosynthetic autotrophs, unicellular algae and diatoms. Some protists are heterotrophic, 𝑒. 𝑔., Protozoa.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Among plants ‘pheromones’ are secreted by the cells of the following plants for given function

options.A: Ll plants for growth and development

Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** Pheromone is a substance secreted to outside by an individual and received by a second individual of the same species in which it induces a specific reaction, 𝑒. 𝑔., fusion of two yeast cells during sexual reproduction.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 differs form 𝐸𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 in having
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Contractile vacuoles are required foe osmoregulation, 𝑖. 𝑒., maintenance of water balance within the body. These are found in the cytoplasm of those organisms, which live in hypotonic water. 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎is a good example of such type of organisms. 𝐸𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎, an endoparasite, lives in the large intestine where the surrounding is isotonic. The osmotic concentration of its body protoplasm equals to that of the intestinal fluid of the host and hence no water enters the parasite by osmosis. So, this organism does not require contractile vacuoles.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Consider the following statements about sexual reproduction I. In class-Phycomycetes, sexual reproduction produces a resting diploid spore called zygospore II. Zygospores are formed by the fusion of two gametes III. These gametes are similar in morphology or dissimilar Which of the statements given above are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** In Phycomycetes, zoospores are formed by the fusion of two gametes. These gametes are similar (isogamous) or dissimilar (anisogamous or oogamous) in morphology
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝑁𝑖𝑓 genes occur in
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** 𝑅ℎ𝑖𝑧𝑜𝑏𝑖𝑢𝑚 𝑙𝑒𝑔𝑢𝑚𝑖𝑛𝑜𝑠𝑎𝑟𝑢𝑚is a nitrogen fixing bacterium found symbiotically within the root nodules of leguminous plants. In 𝑅ℎ𝑖𝑧𝑜𝑏𝑖𝑢𝑚, 𝑵𝒊𝒇 genesare present, which are responsible for the synthesis of enzymes nitrogenous and has the capability of fixing atmospheric nitrogen.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Consider the following statements about Deuteromycetes I. Some members are saprophytes or parasites II. A large number of members are decomposers of litter and help in mineral cycling III. 𝐴𝑙𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑛𝑎𝑟𝑖𝑎, 𝐶𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑡𝑜𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑐ℎ𝑢𝑚, 𝐶𝑒𝑟𝑐𝑜𝑠𝑝𝑜𝑟𝑎 and 𝑇𝑟𝑖𝑐ℎ𝑜𝑑𝑒𝑟𝑚𝑎 are examples of Deuteromycetes Which of the above are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** Deuteromycetes are saprotrophs in soil and on decaying organic matter. Most of them become parasites and cause serious diseases in plants, animals and human beings. A large number of Deuteromycetes are decomposers of litter and help in mineral cycling. Some common examples of Deuteromycetes are; Alternaria, Colletotricum, Fusarium, Trichoderma, Cercospora, etc
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Find out the pairs, which are correctly matched? I. Cyanobacteria –Biopesticides II. Mycorrhiza – Solubilization of phosphate III. 𝐵𝑎𝑐𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑢𝑠 𝑡ℎ𝑢𝑟𝑖𝑛𝑔𝑖𝑒𝑛𝑠𝑖𝑠 – 𝑐𝑟𝑦 protein IV. Single cell protein – Rhizobia
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** Fungus of mycorrhiza helps in solubilization of phosphate. 𝐵𝑎𝑐𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑢𝑠 𝑡ℎ𝑢𝑟𝑖𝑛𝑔𝑖𝑒𝑛𝑠𝑖𝑠has𝑐𝑟𝑦 gene responsible for synthesis of cry protein.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝑇ℎ𝑒𝑟𝑚𝑜𝑐𝑜𝑐𝑐𝑢𝑠, 𝑀𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑎𝑛𝑜𝑐𝑜𝑐𝑐𝑢𝑠 and 𝑀𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑎𝑛𝑜𝑏𝑎𝑐−𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑖𝑢𝑚 exemplify

options.A: Rchaebacteria that contain protein homologous to eukaryotic core histones
options.B: Archaebacteria that lack any histones resembling those found in eukaryotes but whose DNA is negatively supercoiled
options.C: Bacteria whose DNA is relaxed or positively supercoiled but, which have a cytoskeleton as well as mitochondria
options.D: Bacteria that contain a cytoskeleton and ribosomes

Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Inspection of domain Archaea shows that two sub-divisions exist; the Euryarchaeota and the Crenarchaeota. The Euryarchaeota includes 𝑀𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑎𝑛𝑜𝑏𝑎𝑐𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑖𝑢𝑚, 𝑀𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑎𝑛𝑜𝑐𝑜𝑐𝑐𝑢𝑠, 𝑇ℎ𝑒𝑟𝑚𝑜𝑐𝑜𝑐𝑐𝑢𝑠.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Consider the following statement about plants I. Kingdom-Plantae includes eukaryotic autotrophic, chlorophyll containing organisms II. It includes algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms but not angiosperms III. Plants shows alternation of generation [between haploid gametophytic (𝑛) phase and diploid sporophytic (2𝑛) phase] Which of the statements given above are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** The plant cell have an eukaryotic structure with prominent chloroplast. Chloroplast contains chlorophyll which is responsible for the plant’s green colour and imparts the ability to absorb energy from sunlight. This energy is used to convert water plus atmospheric carbon dioxide into metabolisable sugars by the biochemical process of photosynthesis. Kingdom includes algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms. Life cycle consists of alternating haploid gametophyte and diploid sporophyte generations
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: The structure in 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 functionally similar to human kidney is
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎has only one contractile vacuole. This vacuole regularly pumps out excess water like human kidney.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Consider the following statements about mycoplasma I. It is pleuomorphic bacteria, which lacks cell wall II. Mycoplasma is the smallest living organism III. They can not survive without oxygen IV. Many mycoplasma are pathogenic in animals and plants Which of the statements given above are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** Mycoplasmas are the simplest and the smallest of the free living prokaryotes. Due to the absence of cell wall, the organisms can change their shape and are pleomorphic. They can survive without oxygen. Many mycoplasma are pathogenic in animals and plants. They mostly produce pleuropneumonia in domestic animals, a typical pneumonia and mycoplasmal urethritis in humans, little leaf disease of brinjal and witches broom in plants
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Consider the following statements about slime moulds I. 𝑃𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑢𝑚 is found in acellular slime moulds II. Pseudoplasmodium is found in cellular slime moulds Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** Plasmodium is a free-living multinucleate amoeboid mass of protoplasm. It is found in acellular slime moulds. Pseudoplasmodium is an aggregated mass of amoeboid cells where each cell maintains its separate identify. Pseudoplasmodium is found in cellular slime moulds
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Consider the following statements about class-Oomycetes? I. Member may be obligate parasite on plants II. The mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic III. Asexual reproduction involves the formation of spore containing sac or sporangia. In aquatic conditions, the sporangia produces zoospores Which of the statements given above are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** Members of class-Oomycetes are found in aquatic habitats and on decaying wood in moist and damp places or as obligate parasites on plants. Thallus is mycelial. The hypae are coenocytic (i.e., aseptate and multinucleate). Asexual reproduction occurs by the formation of spores produced inside the sac-like sporangia. Terrestrial species produces aplanospores and aquatic species produces zoospores
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: The hyphae of 𝑅ℎ𝑖𝑧𝑜𝑝𝑢𝑠 are
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** The plant body of the 𝑅ℎ𝑖𝑧𝑜𝑝𝑢𝑠 is mycelium which is eucarpic. The mycelium is distinguishable into three types of hyphae namely rhizoidal hyphae, stolons and sporangiophores. The mycelium is aspetate, branched and multinucleate (coenocytic).
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝑁𝑜𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑐 and 𝐴𝑛𝑎𝑏𝑎𝑒𝑛𝑎 belongs to
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** Nitrogen fixing cyanobacteria are often used for reclaiming USAR soils, 𝑒. 𝑔., Nostoc, Anabaena. These cyanobacteria produce acidic chemicals for counteracting alkalinity of the soil and nitrogenous compounds, which are generally deficient in these soils
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝐶𝑙𝑎𝑣𝑖𝑐𝑒𝑝𝑠 is a member of
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** 𝐶𝑙𝑎𝑣𝑖𝑐𝑒𝑝𝑠is a member of class-Ascomycetes. The Ascomycetes have a multicellular mycelium (except yeast) with septal pore and chitinous wall. The sexual reproduction produces dikaryophase (𝑛+ 𝑛). Other examples are: 𝑆𝑎𝑐𝑐ℎ𝑎𝑟𝑜𝑚𝑦𝑐𝑒𝑠, 𝑃𝑒𝑛𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑖𝑢𝑚, 𝐴𝑠𝑝𝑒𝑟𝑔𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑢𝑠, 𝑁𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑜𝑠𝑝𝑜𝑟𝑎, 𝑀𝑜𝑟𝑐ℎ𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑎, etc
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: female 𝐴𝑛𝑜𝑝ℎ𝑒𝑙𝑒𝑠 mosquito can be recognized by

options.A: Proboscis and palpi are long and more or less of equal length
options.D: Both proboscis and palpi are short

Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Female 𝐴𝑛𝑜𝑝ℎ𝑒𝑙𝑒𝑠 mosquitoesare blood suckers of vertebrates. These have long proboscis and palpi of equal length.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝑃𝑎𝑟𝑎𝑚𝑒𝑐𝑖𝑢𝑚 I. is a ciliated protozoan II. has a cavity that opens to the outside the cell surface III. shows water current maintained by cilia which helps the food to be steared into gullet Which of the statement given above are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** Paramecium are aquatic, actively moving organism because of the presence of cilia. Paramecium have a cavity (gullet) that opens to the outside of the cell surface. The coordinated movement of rows of cilia causes the water laden with food to be steared into the cavity (gullet)
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Identify the label 𝐴, 𝐵, 𝐶 and 𝐷 in the following figures
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **NCERT Explanation:** Option (A) is the correct answer based on NCERT Biology principles for *Biological Classification*.

Biological Classification.question: In 𝑉𝑜𝑟𝑡𝑖𝑐𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑎, the total number of micronuclei formed at the end of pre-zygotic nuclear division in female gamete is
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** In 𝑉𝑎𝑟𝑡𝑖𝑐𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑎, in macroconjugant, micronucleus undergoes two divisions forming 4 nuclei (or micronuclei), 3 of which disintegrate and the remaining one becomes the female pronucleus.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Consider the following statement about kingdom-Animalia I. They are heterotrophic, eukaryotic, multicellular organisms II. Cells do not have cell walls III. Mode of nutrition is holozoic Which of the statements given above are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** Animals are heterotrophic, eukaryotic, multicellular organism. Animal cells do not have cell walls. Nutrition is typically holotrophic. Digestion occurs within specialised cavities
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Consider the following statements I. Kingdom-Protista forms a link between monerans and the other organisms like plants, animal and fungi II. Protists reproduce asexually and sexually by a process involving cell fusion and zygote formation III. Being eukaryotes, the protistan cell body contains a well defined nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles Which of the statements given above are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** Phylogenetically the kingdom-Protista acts as a connecting link between the prokaryotic kingdom-Monera on one hand and the complex multicellular kingdoms-Fungi, Plantae and Animalia on the other hand. Protists reproduce asexually and sexually by a process involving cell fusion and zygote formation. Eukaryotes means true nucleus bearing organisms
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: The ‘witches broom’ is caused by a
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** Witches broom is a disease of cherries caused by 𝑇𝑎𝑝ℎ𝑟𝑖𝑛𝑎 𝑐𝑒𝑟𝑎𝑠𝑖, a member of fungal class- Ascomycetes.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝑇𝑟𝑖𝑎𝑡𝑜𝑚𝑎 𝑖𝑛𝑓𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑛𝑠 is the intermediate host in the life cycle of
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** 𝑇𝑟𝑦𝑝𝑎𝑛𝑜𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑎 𝑐𝑟𝑢𝑧𝑖is the digenetic parasite 𝑖. 𝑒., its life cycle is completed into two hosts. The primary host is man, cat, dog or monkey and secondary or intermediate host of this parasite is 𝑇𝑟𝑖𝑎𝑡𝑜𝑚𝑎 𝑖𝑛𝑓𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑛𝑠.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Members of Phycomycetes are found I. In aquatic habitats II. on decaying wood III. in moist and damp places IV. as obligate parasite on plants Which of the statements given above are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Members of Phycomycetes are found in aquatic habitats and on decaying wood in moist and damp places or as obligate parasites on plants
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝑃𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑢𝑚 is an
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** 𝑃𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑢𝑚is a causative agent of malaria disease. It is an endoparasite (present within the body) and interacellular parasite.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝑀𝑢𝑐𝑜𝑟 and 𝑅ℎ𝑖𝑧𝑜𝑝𝑢𝑠 are included in class
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** Mucor (dung mould) and Rhizopus (black bread mould) are included in class-Phycomycetes. Both are the common saprotrophic fungi, that attack a variety of food stuffs
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: On the basis of their shape, bacteria are grouped under…categories
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** Bacteria are grouped under four categories based on their shape. The spherical coccus, the rod- shaped bacillus, the comma-shaped vibrium and the spiral spirillum
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: In 𝑃𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑢𝑚, ookinete is formed by
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** The motile zygote formed by fertilization (anisogamy) of macrogamete by a microgamete is called ookinete.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝑃𝑎𝑟𝑎𝑚𝑒𝑐𝑖𝑢𝑚 is an aquatic and actively moving organism due to the presence of
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** The most characteristic feature of Paramecium is the presence of a large number of cilia on the whole body surface. Paramecium uses cilia for locomotion and capturing food
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: In the diagram, which of the following process is/are shown in 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** The mode of nutrition in 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 is holozoic and involves the following processes: (a) Phagocytosis, 𝑖. 𝑒., intake of food in solid form. (b) Pinocytosis, 𝑖. 𝑒., intake of food in liquid or solution form. (c) Exocytosis, 𝑖. 𝑒., egestion of residual undigested food. Figure in the question shows all the three process stated above.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝐸𝑢𝑔𝑙𝑒𝑛𝑎 is found in
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** Euglena is found in fresh and stagnant water
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: The bacteria 𝑃𝑠𝑒𝑢𝑑𝑜𝑚𝑜𝑛𝑎𝑠 is useful because of its ability to

options.A: Transfer genes from one plant to another
options.C: Fix atmospheric nitrogen in the soil
options.D: Produced a wide variety of antibiotics

Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** The bacteria 𝑃𝑠𝑒𝑢𝑑𝑜𝑚𝑜𝑛𝑎𝑠 is useful because of its ability to decompose a variety of organic compounds. Prof. Anand Mohan Chakraworty (an Indian born Molecular Biologist) developed a super strain of 𝑃𝑠𝑒𝑢𝑑𝑜𝑚𝑜𝑛𝑎𝑠, which can degrade oil. It is known as Chakraworty’s superbug.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Consider the following statements I. Bacteria reproduce only by binary fission II. Under unfavourable conditions, bacteria produce several types of spores III. Bacteria reproduce by a sort of sexual reproduction by adopting a primitive type of RNA transfer from one bacterium to other Which of the statements given below are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** Binary fission is the common method of bacterial multiplication under favourable conditions. Bacteria produces several types of spores called gonidia, sporangiophores, arthrospores, canidia, cysts and endospores. Bacteria also reproduce by a sort of sexual reproduction by adopting a primitive type of DNA transfer from one bacterium to the other
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 is a/an
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎is an unicellular, microscopic organism measuring 250 −500μ. It is a free living protozoan found in ponds, drains ditches and springs, etc.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Amoeboid protozoans I. live in freshwater, sea water or moist soil II. has pseudopodia for locomotion and capturing prey III. have silica shells on their surface in marine forms Which of the statements given above are correct?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** Amoeboid protozoans lives in freshwater, sea water moist soil, They move and capture their prey by putting out pseudopodia. Marine amoeboid protozoans have silica shells on their surface
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Encysted, non-motile and non-feeding infectious stage of 𝐸𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 ℎ𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑙𝑦𝑡𝑖𝑐𝑎 is called
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** Encysted, non-feeding and non-motile infectious stage of 𝐸𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 is called minuta form.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Consider the following statements about Ascomycetes I. They are saprophytic, decomposer, coprophilous and parasitic II. Includes unicellular and multicellular forms III. Mycelium is coenocytic and aseptate IV. 𝐴𝑠𝑝𝑒𝑟𝑔𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑢𝑠, 𝐶𝑙𝑎𝑣𝑖𝑐𝑒𝑝𝑠, 𝑁𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑜𝑠𝑝𝑜𝑟𝑎 are important examples of Ascomycetes Which of the statements given above is/are false?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** All are correct except III. In Ascomycetes, the mycelium is well developed and branched. The hyphae are septate and multicellular
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: What happens in anterior part of 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 at the time of formation of pseudopodia?

options.A: Plasma gel is converted into plasma sol.
options.B: Plasma sol is converted into plasma gel.
options.C: Ectoplasm is converted into endoplasm. P a g e | 36

Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** At the time of formation of pseudopodia in anterior part of 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎, plasma sol is converted into plasma gel.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: How many young amoebae hatch out from a cyst of 𝐸. ℎ𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑙𝑦𝑡𝑖𝑐𝑎?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** In the new host, after 5-6 hours, cyst wall is digested releasing the tetranucleate 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 called excystic 𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 or metacyst.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Halophilic archaebacterium, 𝑒𝑔, 𝐻𝑎𝑙𝑜𝑏𝑎𝑐𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑖𝑢𝑚 𝑠𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑛𝑎𝑟𝑢𝑚 found in great salt lake and dead sea cannot live in
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Archaebacterium cannot live in less than 3M NaCl concentration.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: During conjugation in 𝑃𝑎𝑟𝑎𝑚𝑒𝑐𝑖𝑢𝑚

options.A: Out of the four micronuclei formed, three degenerate
options.B: Out of six macronuclei formed, four degenerate
options.C: Zygote nucleus undergoes eight successive division in each conjugant

Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** During conjugation in 𝑃𝑎𝑟𝑎𝑚𝑒𝑐𝑖𝑢𝑚, the micronucleus undergoes successive divisions one of which is meiosis. The four haploid daughter nuclei are formed out of them three degenerate and one divides from them and form two gametic nuclei one male and one female.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Carries of 𝐸𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 ℎ𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑙𝑦𝑡𝑖𝑐𝑎 are
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** 𝐸𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 ℎ𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑘𝑦𝑡𝑖𝑐𝑎is a microscopic endoparasite of man. It is commonly found in the upper part of large intestine and is very often lodged in liver, lungs, brain and testes. It invades the mucosa and submucosa of the intestinal wall and causes amoebic dysentery or amoebiasis. Infection depends upon intake of food or water contaminated with faecal matter. Houseflies sitting on faecal matter of hosts containing cysts may transfer them to food stuff.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Nutrition of 𝐸𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑚𝑜𝑒𝑏𝑎 is
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** 𝐸. ℎ𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑙𝑦𝑡𝑖𝑐𝑎is a microscopic endoparasite found in the lumen of upper part of large intestine, 𝑖. 𝑒., colon. Parasitologists believe that this this parasite lives there as harmless commensal but due to unknown reasons they invade the mucosa and submucosa of the intestinal wall and cause amoebic dysentery or amoebiasis.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Chlorophyll-𝛼 absent, in which of the following photosynthetic organisms?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** The photosynthetic bacteria contain bacteriochlorophyll but lack chlorophyll-𝑎.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Name the class of the Mycota which is commonly called ‘fungi imperfecti’?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Deuteromycota is commonly called as fungi imperfecti. This includes all those fungi in which sexual or perfect stage is not known.
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Yeast and 𝑃𝑒𝑛𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑖𝑢𝑚 are the example of class
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** Morels, truffles, yeast and Penicillium are all examples of class-Ascomycetes. Yeast is single cell member of class-Ascomycetes. Penicillium is a genus of fungi, commonly growing as green or blue moulds on decaying food, used in making medicine (antibiotics)
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: ….. include blue-green algae, which have chlorophyll-𝑎 similar to green plants. Complete the given sentence with an appropriate option
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** Photosynthetic autotrophic bacteria includes blue-green algae, which have chlorophyll-a similar to the green plants
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: The given statements describes a group of organisms I. The pellicle is composed of fibrous elastic protein lipid or carbohydrates and maintains a definite shape II. They have two flagella, short and a long one. Each flagellum arises from a basal granule III. They are connecting link between plants and animals Which of the following group is referred here?
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Euglenoids are unicellular flagellate protists. They are without cellulosic cell wall. The body is covered by thin and flexible pellicle. The pellicle is composed of fibrous elastin protein, small amount of lipid or/and carbohydrates. The euglenoids have two flagella, usually one long and one short. Each flagellum arises from a basal granule (blepharoplast). The flagella bear hairs (=tinsels). They are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight. They are considered as connecting link between plants and animals
Biological Classification.subject: Biology

Biological Classification.question: Kingdom-Animalia organisms I. are capable of Iocomotion II. have specialised sensory and neuromotor system III. shows sexual mode of reproduction IV. show the sexual reproduction by copulation of male and female followed by embryological development Which of the statements given above are correct
Biological Classification.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** Most animals have the ability to move fairly freely. Animals have specialised sensory and neuromotor system. Reproduction is generally sexual. Gamates are formed, mostly in multicellular organs called gonads (ovaries or testes). Lower forms performs asexual reproduction also. The sexual reproduction takes place by copulation of male and female followed by embryological developement

Plant Kingdom.question: [NEET 2022 | Biology] In bryophytes, the dominant plant body is:
Plant Kingdom.solution: ## **Correct Answer: (B) Gametophyte (haploid)** --- ## **Step-by-Step Reasoning:** ### Life Cycle of Bryophytes: 1. **Gametophytic Generation (Haploid, n)** - The moss plant you see growing on rocks/soil - Independent, free-living, photosynthetic - Produces male (antheridia) and female (archegonia) gametes - Larger and more conspicuous 2. **Sporophytic Generation (Diploid, 2n)** - Develops after fertilization - Attached to and dependent on the gametophyte - Consists of: foot, seta (stalk), and capsule - Produces spores (not independent) - Smaller and temporary --- ## **Why This is Important (Key Concept):** | Feature | Gametophyte | Sporophyte | |---------|------------|-----------| | **Ploidy** | Haploid (n) | Diploid (2n) | | **Independence** | Independent \u₂₇₁₃ | Dependent \u₂₇₁₇ | | **Dominance** | **DOMINANT** | Reduced | | **Photosynthesis** | Yes | Yes, but limited | | **Lifestyle** | Perennial | Temporary | --- ## **Why Other Options Are Wrong:** - **(A) Sporophyte dominant:** False. The sporophyte is small, dependent, and temporary in bryophytes. This is true for *seed plants*, not bryophytes. - **(C) Both equally dominant:** False. There's a clear dominance of gametophyte; sporophyte is clearly subordinate. - **(D) Neither \— haplodiplontic:** Haplodiplontic means alternation of EQUAL generations (like in many algae). In bryophytes, it's **haplontic dominant** (gametophyte-dominant). --- ## **Memory Tip:** **"Bryophytes = Baby sporophytes"** The sporophyte is like a dependent "baby" still attached to its parent gametophyte!
Plant Kingdom.subject: Biology

Plant Kingdom.question: [NEET 2020 | Biology] In which organism do gametophytes NOT have free-living independent existence?
Plant Kingdom.solution: # Answer: **(D) Pinus** --- ## Step-by-Step Explanation ### Comparing Gametophyte Independence Across Organisms: | Organism | Type | Gametophyte Status | |----------|------|-------------------| | **Pteris** | Fern (Seedless vascular) | Free-living prothallus \u₂₇₁₃ | | **Marchantia** | Liverwort (Bryophyte) | Free-living plant body \u₂₇₁₃ | | **Funaria** | Moss (Bryophyte) | Free-living plant body \u₂₇₁₃ | | **Pinus** | Gymnosperm (Seed plant) | Reduced, embedded, dependent \u₂₇₁₇ | --- ## Why Pinus is Correct ### Gametophytes in Pinus: - **Male gametophyte**: Pollen grain (only 2-3 cells) - enclosed in sporophyte anther - **Female gametophyte**: Endosperm tissue - embedded within the ovule **Key Point**: Both are: - Highly reduced - Embedded within sporophyte tissues - Completely dependent on sporophyte for: - Protection - Nutrition - Water - Physical support - **NOT capable of independent survival** --- ## Why Others Are Wrong **(A) Pteris**: Fern gametophyte (prothallus) is a small, green, independent plant that can photosynthesize and survive alone. **(B) Marchantia**: Liverwort gametophyte IS the main plant body - it's independent and free-living. **(C) Funaria**: Moss gametophyte (leafy moss) IS the dominant phase - independent and free-living. --- ## Key Concept to Remember ``` Bryophytes & Seedless Vascular Plants \u₂₁₉₂ Gametophyte DOMINANT & FREE-LIVING Seed Plants (Gymnosperms & Angiosperms) \u₂₁₉₂ Gametophyte REDUCED & DEPENDENT ``` In the evolutionary trend toward seed plants, gametophytes became increasingly reduced and lost independence - they're now merely reproductive structures embedded in the sporophyte!
Plant Kingdom.subject: Biology

Animal Kingdom.question: [NEET 2022 | Biology] Which have an open circulatory system?
Animal Kingdom.solution: ## **Correct Answer: (D) Cockroach and prawn** --- ## **Step-by-Step Reasoning:** ### **Circulatory Systems Overview:** | Organism | Circulatory Type | Details | |----------|------------------|---------| | **Earthworm** | **Closed** | Blood confined in vessels; contracts aortic arches pump blood | | **Cockroach** | **Open** | Blood (hemolymph) bathes organs directly in body cavity | | **Prawn** | **Open** | Blood (hemolymph) circulates through hemocoel | --- ## **Why Each Option is Correct/Incorrect:** | Option | Analysis | |--------|----------| | **(A) Earthworm** | \u₂₇₄c WRONG - Earthworms have a **closed** circulatory system | | **(B) Cockroach only** | \u₂₇₄c WRONG - Incomplete answer; prawn also has open circulation | | **(C) Prawn only** | \u₂₇₄c WRONG - Incomplete answer; cockroach also has open circulation | | **(D) Cockroach and prawn** | \u₂₇₀₅ **CORRECT** - Both are arthropods with open circulation | --- ## **Key Concept to Remember:** **ARTHROPODS = OPEN CIRCULATORY SYSTEM** - Cockroach, Prawn, Insects, Spiders, all arthropods have **hemocoel** (body cavity) - Blood flows freely around organs - Less efficient but requires lower metabolic rate **ANNELIDS = CLOSED CIRCULATORY SYSTEM** - Earthworms have true blood vessels - Blood contained in closed loops - More efficient oxygen transport --- ## **Quick Memory Tip:** \U₀₀₀₁f₅₃₄ **"Arthropods are OPEN house parties"** - their blood flows freely everywhere!
Animal Kingdom.subject: Biology

Animal Kingdom.question: [NEET 2019 | Biology] Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Chordata?
Animal Kingdom.solution: # Answer: **(D) Ventral heart** ## Why This Is The Answer The **three PRIMARY diagnostic characteristics of Chordata** are: 1. **Notochord** (A) \u₂₇₁₃₂. **Dorsal hollow nerve cord** (B) \u₂₇₁₃₃. **Pharyngeal gill slits** (C) \u₂₇₁₃ While it's TRUE that chordates have a **ventral heart**, this is NOT typically listed as one of the defining characteristics of the phylum Chordata in standard NCERT biology. --- ## Key Concept to Remember **The Three Defining Features of Chordata** (appear at some stage in all chordates): | Feature | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Notochord** | Flexible rod providing body support (replaced by vertebral column in vertebrates) | | **Dorsal Hollow Nerve Cord** | Nerve cord on the DORSAL (back) side, hollow throughout | | **Pharyngeal Gill Slits** | Present in pharynx at some developmental stage | --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong - **(A) Notochord** - This is THE defining feature of all chordates - **(B) Dorsal hollow nerve cord** - Universal chordate feature - **(C) Pharyngeal gill slits** - Universal feature (even humans have pharyngeal pouches as embryos) - **(D) Ventral heart** - While TRUE in chordates, it's NOT a primary diagnostic criterion --- ## Exam Tip \U₀₀₀₁f₄a₁ Remember: When NEET asks about chordate characteristics, focus on the **"Big 3"** - Notochord, Dorsal Nerve Cord, and Pharyngeal Gill Slits. These are non-negotiable!
Animal Kingdom.subject: Biology

Morphology of Flowering Plants.question: [NEET 2019 | Biology] Megasporangium is ≡alent to:
Morphology of Flowering Plants.solution: # Megasporangium Equivalence **Correct Answer: (B) Ovule** ## Step-by-Step Explanation: ### What is a Megasporangium? - **Megasporangium** = the tissue that produces megaspores (female reproductive spores) - In flowering plants, it's essentially the **nucellus** (central tissue of the ovule) ### Structure of an Ovule: An ovule consists of three main parts: 1. **Integuments** - outer protective layer(s) 2. **Nucellus** - inner tissue (= megasporangium) 3. **Embryo sac** - develops from megaspore ### Why Ovule is the Answer: - The **ovule is functionally and structurally ≡alent to the megasporangium** in flowering plants - The megasporangium is the reproductive tissue WITHIN the ovule - The ovule as a whole structure serves the same reproductive function as megasporangium in lower plants ## Why Other Options Are Wrong: | Option | Why It's Wrong | |--------|---| | **(A) Fruit** | Fruit develops AFTER fertilization; megasporangium is pre-fertilization female structure | | **(C) Seed** | Seed develops from ovule AFTER fertilization; megasporangium precedes this | | **(D) Leaf** | Leaf is vegetative; megasporangium is reproductive tissue | ## Key Fact to Remember: **Ovule = Megasporangium + Integuments** The ovule is the female reproductive organ, and its functional core is the megasporangium.
Morphology of Flowering Plants.subject: Biology

Morphology of Flowering Plants.question: [NEET 2021 | Biology] According to Lindemann's 10% law, if a herbivore gets 100 J of energy, how much energy will be available to a primary carnivore?
Morphology of Flowering Plants.solution: ## Correct Answer: **(B) 10 J** --- ## Step-by-Step Reasoning: **Energy Transfer Chain:** - Producer (Plant) → Herbivore → Primary Carnivore (Secondary Consumer) **Applying Lindemann's 10% Law:** - Energy available to Herbivore = 100 J (given) - Energy transferred to Primary Carnivore = 10% of 100 J - = 0.10 × 100 J = **10 J** --- ## The Underlying Concept: **Lindemann's 10% Law** states that: - Only **10% of the energy** from one trophic level is transferred to the next trophic level - The remaining **90% is lost** through: - Cellular respiration (metabolism) - Heat dissipation - Excretion - Decomposition of dead organisms **General Formula:** ``` Energy at level n+1 = 10% of Energy at level n or E(n+1) = 0.1 × E(n) ``` --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong: | Option | Why It's Wrong | |--------|---| | (A) 100 J | This would mean 100% energy transfer - impossible as energy is always lost | | (C) 1 J | This would be 10% of 10 J (third trophic level), not the primary carnivore | | (D) 50 J | This represents 50% efficiency, which contradicts Lindemann's law | --- ## Key Formula to Remember: 📌 **Energy at trophic level = (0.1)ⁿ × Initial Producer Energy** Where n = number of trophic levels from producer For this problem: Carnivore energy = 0.1 × 100 = **10 J**
Morphology of Flowering Plants.subject: Biology

Morphology of Flowering Plants.question: [NEET 2018 | Biology] Which ecological pyramid is always up (never inverted)?
Morphology of Flowering Plants.solution: ## Answer: **(C) Pyramid of Energy** --- ## Step-by-Step Explanation: ### Why Pyramid of Energy is Always Up: 1. **Energy Flow Rule**: Only approximately **10% of energy** transfers from one trophic level to the next - The remaining 90% is lost through: - Respiration (heat release) - Movement and metabolism - Incomplete consumption - Death and decomposition 2. **Mathematical Certainty**: - If Producers have = 10,000 kcal - Primary consumers get ≈ 1,000 kcal - Secondary consumers get ≈ 100 kcal - Tertiary consumers get ≈ 10 kcal **This gradient can NEVER reverse** 3. **Thermodynamic Basis**: - Follows the **Second Law of Thermodynamics** - Energy can never be created, only transferred with loss - Higher trophic levels always have progressively less available energy --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong: | Type | Can Be Inverted? | Example | |------|------------------|---------| | **(A) Pyramid of Numbers** | ✗ YES, inverted possible | 1 oak tree → 1000s of insects → 1000s of parasites | | **(B) Pyramid of Biomass** | ✗ YES, inverted possible | Phytoplankton (small, numerous) → Large fish (few, heavy) | | **(D) All can be inverted** | ✗ WRONG | Energy pyramid cannot be inverted | --- ## Key Formula to Remember: **Energy Transfer = 10% Rule** Energy at Level n+1 = Energy at Level n × 0.10 This ensures the pyramid always narrows upward! 📈
Morphology of Flowering Plants.subject: Biology

Morphology of Flowering Plants.question: [NEET 2023 | Biology] In double fertilisation, triple fusion involves fusion of one male gamete with:
Morphology of Flowering Plants.solution: # Triple Fusion in Double Fertilization ## **Correct Answer: (B) Two polar nuclei** --- ## Step-by-Step Explanation ### What is Double Fertilization? In flowering plants, the mature embryo sac contains **8 nuclei**: - **Egg apparatus**: 1 egg cell + 2 synergids - **Central cell**: 2 polar nuclei - **Antipodal cells**: 3 antipodal nuclei ### The Two Fertilization Events: | Event | Fusion | Product | Ploidy | |-------|--------|---------|--------| | **First Fertilization** | 1 male gamete (n) + Egg cell (n) | Zygote | 2n | | **Triple Fusion** | 1 male gamete (n) + **2 Polar nuclei (n+n)** | Primary Endosperm Nucleus | 3n | ### Why It's Called "Triple Fusion" The name comes from **3 nuclei** participating: - 1 male gamete nucleus - 2 polar nuclei from the central cell - = **3n endosperm** (triploid - nutritive tissue) --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong: **(A) Egg cell** - This fuses with ONE male gamete in the FIRST fertilization, not triple fusion **(C) One polar nucleus and egg** - This is not a real fusion event in the process **(D) Two synergids** - Synergids are **degenerate help cells** in the egg apparatus; they don't participate in fertilization --- ## Key Fact to Remember: **Triple fusion = Male gamete + Central cell (2 polar nuclei)** - Result: **3n endosperm** (stores nutrients for developing embryo)
Morphology of Flowering Plants.subject: Biology

Morphology of Flowering Plants.question: [NEET 2021 | Biology] Pneumatophores are found in:
Morphology of Flowering Plants.solution: ## **Correct Answer: (A) Mangrove plants** --- ## **What are Pneumatophores?** Pneumatophores are **specialized aerial roots** that grow upward above the soil/water surface. They are: - **Negatively geotropic** (grow against gravity) - Covered with **lenticels** (pores for gas exchange) - Spongy with **aerenchyma tissue** (air spaces) --- ## **Why Mangrove Plants Need Them?** Mangroves live in: - **Waterlogged, anaerobic soils** (coastal tidal zones) - **Saline environments** with poor oxygen availability The waterlogged soil cannot supply sufficient oxygen to roots, so pneumatophores: 1. Grow upward into air-rich atmosphere 2. Absorb oxygen through lenticels 3. Transport it down to underground roots 4. Keep the plant alive in hostile conditions **Classic examples:** *Avicennia*, *Rhizophora*, *Bruguiera* --- ## **Why Other Options Are Wrong:** | Option | Why It's Wrong | |--------|---| | **(B) Desert plants** | Desert soil is well-drained and oxygen-rich; they need water conservation, not pneumatophores | | **(C) Aquatic plants** | Some use **aerenchyma** tissue instead; not typically pneumatophores | | **(D) Parasitic plants** | No special oxygen requirements; nutrients obtained from host | --- ## **Key Formula/Fact to Remember:** **Pneumatophore = Oxygen-bearing aerial root for anaerobic/waterlogged environments** \u₂₇₁₃ **NEET Tip:** When you see "mangrove adaptation" questions, always think of pneumatophores!
Morphology of Flowering Plants.subject: Biology

Morphology of Flowering Plants.question: Based on a 10% law of energy transfer, identify values for A, B, and C in the figure given below.
Morphology of Flowering Plants.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** The 10% law was proposed by Lindemann in 1942. The transfer of energy from one trophic level to another trophic level is accompanied by loss of energy at each level or step. When the plants are eaten by the herbivore, approximately 10% of energy in the food is fixed into animal flesh, whereas 90% is consumed in ingestion, respiration, maintenance of body heat and other activities. Similarly, when a carnivore consumes that herbivore, again approimately 10% of energy is fixed. Therefore, at each transfer, only 10% of the total energy is actually available to the next trophic level. It is called 10% law. **Key Point:** Always read all options carefully and eliminate wrong ones using fundamental NCERT concepts.

Morphology of Flowering Plants.question: [NEET 2020 | Biology] Which is NOT a functional unit of ecosystem?
Morphology of Flowering Plants.solution: # Answer: **(D) Stratification** ## Explanation **Stratification is a STRUCTURAL feature**, not a functional unit of an ecosystem. ### Key Distinction: | **Functional Units** | **Structural Features** | |---|---| | Dynamic processes that keep ecosystem working | Static organization of ecosystem | | Energy flow, nutrient cycling, decomposition | Stratification, biodiversity patterns | ### Why Each Option Works (Except D): | Option | Why it's Functional | |---|---| | **(A) Energy Flow** | Primary functional unit - movement of energy from sun \u₂₁₉₂ producers \u₂₁₉₂ consumers | | **(B) Decomposition** | Functional process breaking down dead matter and recycling nutrients | | **(C) Productivity** | Functional measure - how much biomass/energy is created (NPP, GPP) | | **(D) Stratification** | \u₂₇₄c Only describes **layering/vertical arrangement** (structural), not how ecosystem functions | ## Example: - **Stratification** = A forest has canopy, understory, and ground layer (STRUCTURE) - **Energy Flow** = How energy moves through these layers (FUNCTION) ## Key Formula to Remember: **Functional Units = Processes that maintain ecosystem** - Energy flow - Nutrient cycling - Decomposition - Productivity - Food chains/webs --- **NEET Tip:** When in doubt, ask: "Does this describe HOW the ecosystem WORKS (functional) or HOW it's ORGANIZED (structural)?" Stratification = Organization = Structural \u₂₇₁₃
Morphology of Flowering Plants.subject: Biology

Morphology of Flowering Plants.question: [NEET 2020 | Biology] Cork cambium is an example of:
Morphology of Flowering Plants.solution: # Cork Cambium - Meristem Classification ## **Correct Answer: (B) Lateral meristem** --- ## **Step-by-Step Reasoning:** ### What is Cork Cambium? - Cork cambium (phellogen) is a layer of actively dividing cells - Located in the **outer regions of stems and roots** (beneath the epidermis) - Produces **cork cells (phellem) outward** and **phelloderm inward** ### Why it's a Lateral Meristem: | Feature | Cork Cambium | |---------|-------------| | **Location** | Lateral (side) regions of the plant body | | **Function** | Increases the **diameter/girth** of stem and root | | **Type of growth** | Secondary growth (thickness increase) | | **Orientation** | Cylindrical layer running along the stem/root | --- ## **Understanding the Meristem Types:** | Type | Location | Function | |------|----------|----------| | **Apical** | Root and shoot tips | Increases length (primary growth) | | **Lateral** | Sides of stem/root | Increases diameter (secondary growth) | | **Intercalary** | Between mature tissues | Temporary; leaf base, grass stems | | **Primary** | General term for apical meristems | - | --- ## **Why Other Options Are Wrong:** - **(A) Primary meristem** - Primary meristems are apical, not lateral. Cork cambium is secondary. - **(C) Intercalary meristem** - Located between tissues temporarily; cork cambium is permanent and lateral. - **(D) Apical meristem** - Located at tips; cork cambium is at the sides. --- ## **Key Formula to Remember:** **Lateral meristems = Secondary growth = Increase in diameter/girth** Cork cambium and vascular cambium are the two main lateral meristems! \u₂₇₁₃
Morphology of Flowering Plants.subject: Biology

Morphology of Flowering Plants.question: [NEET 2022 | Biology] Which photosystem is responsible for photolysis of water?
Morphology of Flowering Plants.solution: # Answer: **(B) Photosystem II** --- ## Step-by-Step Explanation ### The Process of Water Photolysis Water photolysis occurs at **Photosystem II (PS-II)** in the thylakoid membrane: | Step | Details | |------|---------| | **Location** | Oxygen-Evolving Complex (OEC) at PS-II | | **Reaction** | 2H\u₂₀₈₂O \u₂₁₉₂ O\u₂₀₈₂ + 4H\u₂₀₇a + 4e\u₂₀₇b | | **Catalyst** | Manganese (Mn) cluster | | **Products** | Oxygen, protons, electrons | ### Why PS-II Specifically? 1. **P₆₈₀ Chlorophyll**: PS-II contains P₆₈₀ (chlorophyll a), which absorbs light at 680 nm 2. **Photoinduced Charge Separation**: Light excites electrons in P₆₈₀, creating a strong oxidizing agent 3. **Water Splitting**: This oxidizing power breaks water molecules to replenish lost electrons 4. **Oxygen Release**: Molecular oxygen is released as a byproduct (waste product from our perspective, essential for aerobic respiration) --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong | Option | Why It's Incorrect | |--------|-------------------| | **(A) PS-I only** | PS-I (P₇₀₀) uses electrons but doesn't split water; it reduces NADP\u₂₀₇a | | **(C) Both PS-I & PS-II** | Only PS-II has the oxygen-evolving complex; PS-I doesn't split water | | **(D) Stroma** | Photolysis occurs in thylakoids, not stroma; Calvin cycle occurs in stroma | --- ## Key Formula to Remember **Z-Scheme (Light Reactions):** ``` Water \u₂₁₉₂ PS-II \u₂₁₉₂ Electron Transport Chain \u₂₁₉₂ PS-I \u₂₁₉₂ NADPH (Photolysis) (Cytochrome b\u₂₀₈₆f) \u₂₁₉₃ O\u₂₀₈₂ released H\u₂₀₇a pumped (ATP synthesis) ``` **Remember**: PS-II splits water; PS-I doesn't!

Anatomy of Flowering Plants.question: Cambium is a type of
Anatomy of Flowering Plants.solution: **Correct Answer: (C)** **Explanation:** Lateral Meristem The meristem occurs on the sides and take part in increasing girth of the plant. Anatomy of Flowering Plants.question: Pith is a central part of the ground tissues generally made up of
Anatomy of Flowering Plants.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** The pith or medulla forms the central region of the stem and root. Usually, the pith of dicot stem is largely parenchymatous. It is devoid of chlorophyll in the mature state. The pith is not distinguishable in the mature state. The pith is not distinguishable in monocot stems.
Anatomy of Flowering Plants.subject: Biology

Anatomy of Flowering Plants.question: Interfascicular cambium is found
Anatomy of Flowering Plants.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** As growth begins, the cells of medullary rays, which lie in between vascular bundles become active and rise to cambial strip called interfascicular cambium constitute cambium.
Anatomy of Flowering Plants.subject: Biology

Anatomy of Flowering Plants.question: Meristematic tissue are

options.B: Mature does not have ability of division
options.C: Premature not having ability of division
options.D: Complex differentiating in xylem, phloem and cambium

Anatomy of Flowering Plants.solution: **Correct Answer: (A)** **Explanation:** Tissue is a group of cells performing a particular function. Tissue are mainly of two types (i) Meristematic tissues These tissues contain immature and young cells that are much active and capable of showing continuous divisions and redivisions. They may be promeristem, primary meristem, secondary meristem, apical meristem, intercalary meristem and lateral meristem. (ii) Permanent tissues These are made up of mature cells, which have lost the capacity to divide and have attained a permanent shape, size and function, e.g., simple (parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma), complex (xylem, phloem) and secretory tissue.
Anatomy of Flowering Plants.subject: Biology

It is used as stopper for bottles, shock absorption and insulation

Anatomy of Flowering Plants.question: Secondary phloem of a dicot root is made up of I. sieve tube II. companion cell III. phloem parenchyma Select the correct option for given statement

Anatomy of Flowering Plants.subject: Biology

Anatomy of Flowering Plants.question: I. These tissue are found as layers or patches II. It consists of cells which are thickened at the corners III. It often contains chloroplast IV. Intercellular spaces are absent V. They provide mechanical support to growing parts of plants The above characters are attributed to
Anatomy of Flowering Plants.solution: **Correct Answer: (B)** **Explanation:** Collenchyma. The collenchyma occurs in layers below the epidermis in dicotyledonous plants. It is found either as a homogenous layer or in patches. It consists of cells which are much thickened at the corners due to the deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin. Collenchymatous cells may be oval, spherical or polygonal and often contain chloroplasts. These cells assimilate food when they contain chloroplasts. Intercellular spaces are absent. They provide mechanical support to the growing parts of the plant such as young stem and petiole of a leaf
Anatomy of Flowering Plants.subject: Biology

Anatomy of Flowering Plants.question: Select the wrong statements I. Primary and secondary phloem gets crushed during secondary growth II. During secondary growth, primary xylem remains more or less intact

Anatomy of Flowering Plants.solution: **Correct Answer: (D)** **Explanation:** The primary xylem is in the centre of the stem, while primary phloem is pushed outward and crushed into the cortex by the significant activity of vascular cambium. While the secondary phloem differentiates from the cells that divide towards the outside of the stem
